content:
Hi everyone! I'm working on a project to formalize finitely presented groups (discussed in #ItaLean 2025 > Projects: Finitely Presented Groups, PR #34236) and I'm realizing I'm having trouble managing the dependencies in an effective way.

So essentially, I've been refactoring the code into separate PRs, and when a PR gets merged after review my code breaks and I've been re-merging the branches but I'm not sure this is best practice.

I think since this was my first project I didn't give much thought as to how it could've been set up optimally, and I was wondering if someone could tell me how to do it better continuing forward or refer me to resources explaining how to do this better.

Thanks!
Also every time I switch branches I have to rebuild and it's been a pain. If anyone has advice on this that would be great also!
Do you mean after a PR is merged into mathlib?

So after your PR hits master you can do lake update inside your repo, this will update mathlib and download a new cache, so you don't need to recompile mathlib but only your project. Then you can remove the declarations that are now in mathlib (if they have the exact same name you will get errors). It's a bit annoying but if your PR are not that big and you bump mathlib relatively often (say once a week, regardless of the status of your PR) it's very doable.
Ok, I will try that going forward thanks!
